newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Feb 11.

text.p: NOTE: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

- With 140 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, editorials in the Hong Kong media concentrated on whether pro-democracy members of municipal councils and district boards will stay in their posts beyond the handover and the possible delayed completion of China Light & Power's Black Point power station.

-- The Beijing-backed TA KUNG PAO said that "Love China, Love Hong Kong" and "supporting the Basic Law and One Country, Two Systems" should be the basic principles when Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa appoints members of the provisional Urban and Regional councils. It said whether or not to keep some appointed seats on the councils was not a question of being democratic or not.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL said China Light & Power should be responsible for most of the financial losses arising from any delay of the Black Point power station project. It said senior government officials who had approved the project should also face disciplinary action.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said that Hong Kong was gradually easing itself out of the British Commonwealth and developing academic and professional links with China and the region to match its business connections. While Hong Kong has a proper mechanism to ensure an equitable and efficient system, what was required now was funding and the vision and flexibility to get the job done, the paper said.
